def-competing-risk-data-cause-specific-h:
## Definition

Fix a finite number $K\ge1$ of causes on a probability space. Let
$T_1,\ldots,T_K$ be measurable event times with values in $[0,\infty)$, and
assume that the minimum is attained by a unique cause almost surely. The
**observed first failure time** and its **cause** are
$$T:=\min_{1\le j\le K}T_j,\qquad D:=\min\{j:T_j=T\}\in\{1,\ldots,K\},$$
so $D$ is the smallest label attaining the minimum. For each $k$,
$$\{D=k\}=\bigcap_{j<k}\{T_k<T_j\}\cap\bigcap_{j>k}\{T_k\le T_j\},$$
which is measurable; the assumed almost-sure uniqueness makes the tie-break
irrelevant except on a null set.
No independence among the latent times $T_j$ is assumed. When an external
right-censoring time $C$ is present, the observation is
$(U,\delta,D^{\mathrm{obs}})$, where $U=\min(T,C)$ and
$\delta=\mathbf 1\{T\le C\}$ as in
[[def-event-time-observation-schemes]], and $D^{\mathrm{obs}}=D$ when
$\delta=1$; the cause label is absent when $\delta=0$. Thus an event tied with
censoring is recorded as an event.

The **all-cause survival function** is $S(t):=\mathbb P(T>t)$ for $t\ge0$.
For $u>0$, write $S(u-):=\mathbb P(T\ge u)$; this is the left limit of $S$
by continuity from above for measures
([[thm-continuity-from-above-for-measures]]). Set $S(0-):=1$.

For each cause $k$, its **event subdistribution measure** and
**cause-specific cumulative-incidence function** are
$$\nu_k(B):=\mathbb P(T\in B,D=k),\qquad F_k(t):=\nu_k([0,t])=\mathbb P(T\le t,D=k).$$
for Borel $B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ and $t\ge0$. The **cause-specific hazard
measure** is the measure with density
$$w(u):=\begin{cases}1/S(u-),&S(u-)>0,\\0,&S(u-)=0\end{cases}$$
relative to $\nu_k$:
$$\Lambda_k(B):=\int_B w(u)\,\nu_k(du),\qquad d\Lambda_k(u)=w(u)\,\nu_k(du).$$
The extension of $u\mapsto S(u-)$ by the constant $1$ for $u<0$ is
nonincreasing on $\mathbb R$ and therefore Borel measurable
([[thm-monotone-real-functions-are-borel-measurable]]), so $w$ is a
nonnegative Borel function and this measure is defined by
[[def-measure-with-density]]. It may have infinite total mass; no finite-horizon
integrability is assumed in this definition.
thm-cause-specific-cumulative-incidence-:
## Statement

For every cause $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$ and every $t\ge0$, the cumulative
incidence decomposes as
$$F_k(t)=\int_{[0,t]}S(u-)\,d\Lambda_k(u).$$
If $\nu_k$ has a Lebesgue density $f_k$ and $S$ is continuous and positive on
$(0,t]$, then $d\Lambda_k(u)=\lambda_k(u)\,du$ for Lebesgue-a.e. $u\in(0,t]$
with $\lambda_k(u):=f_k(u)/S(u)$, and
$$F_k(t)=\int_0^tS(u)\lambda_k(u)\,du.$$
alg-aalen-johansen-cumulative-incidence-:
## Definition

**Input:** A finite sample of $n\ge1$ right-censored records
$(U_i,\delta_i,D_i^{\mathrm{obs}})$ for $K$ causes, using
$U_i=\min(T_i,C_i)$ and $\delta_i=\mathbf 1\{T_i\le C_i\}$ from
[[def-event-time-observation-schemes]]. The observed cause label
$D_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$ is present only when $\delta_i=1$.
Fix a horizon $t\ge0$.

The pointwise population target is
$\psi_t:=(S(t),F_1(t),\ldots,F_K(t))\in\mathbb R^{K+1}$; the algorithm
returns its finite-sample estimate.

For each event time $u\in[0,t]$, define the risk count and cause-specific event
counts by
$$Y(u):=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{U_i\ge u\},\qquad \Delta N_k(u):=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{U_i=u,\delta_i=1,D_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=k\},\qquad \Delta N(u):=\sum_{k=1}^K\Delta N_k(u).$$
All subjects with an event at $u$ are included in $Y(u)$, so tied observed
failures are grouped before updating and $Y(u)\ge\Delta N(u)>0$ at every
event time. Censorings at $u$ do not contribute to $\Delta N(u)$; a subject
with $T_i=C_i=u$ is an event by the stated $T_i\le C_i$ convention.

**Procedure:**

1. List the distinct observed event times $u\le t$ in increasing order, with
   all causes at a common time grouped into the same counts $\Delta N_k(u)$.
2. Initialize $\widehat S(0-)=1$ and $\widehat F_k(0-)=0$ for each cause.
3. At each listed $u$, set
   $$\widehat F_k(u)=\widehat F_k(u-)+\widehat S(u-)\frac{\Delta N_k(u)}{Y(u)},\qquad \widehat S(u)=\widehat S(u-)\left(1-\frac{\Delta N(u)}{Y(u)}\right).$$
4. Keep the estimates constant between event times and return
   $(\widehat S(t),\widehat F_1(t),\ldots,\widehat F_K(t))$.

Equivalently,
$$\widehat S(t)=\prod_{0\le u\le t:\,\Delta N(u)>0}\left(1-\frac{\Delta N(u)}{Y(u)}\right),\qquad \widehat F_k(t)=\sum_{0\le u\le t:\,\Delta N(u)>0}\widehat S(u-)\frac{\Delta N_k(u)}{Y(u)}.$$
The convention at $u=0$ allows a baseline event; when there is none, these
formulas agree with the $(0,t]$ product-limit convention in
[[def-nelson-aalen-kaplan-meier-greenwood-estimators]].

This procedure is a finite-sample definition, not a consistency or variance
theorem. A common sampling setup for interpreting it as an estimator of a
population law has IID subject records ([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]),
independent censoring $C\perp(T,D)$ ([[def-independent-random-elements]]), and
$\mathbb P(C\ge t)>0$, a positive censoring-support condition through $t$.
These are model assumptions, not consequences of the formula.
This item does not invoke a counting-process compensator, martingale bracket,
or process-limit result.
lem-aalen-johansen-fixed-time-output-is-:
## Statement

Fix $n\ge1$, finite $K$, and $t\ge0$. Give the sample space
$$\mathcal X=\big([0,\infty)\times\{0,1,\ldots,K\}\big)^n$$
its Borel sigma-algebra as a Euclidean subspace, where status $0$ denotes
censoring and status $k$ denotes an observed cause-$k$ event. Equip
$\mathbb R^{K+1}$ with its Borel sigma-algebra. The output vector of
[[alg-aalen-johansen-cumulative-incidence-estimator]] at horizon $t$ is a
measurable map $\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^{K+1}$ and hence a statistic. Every
event-time denominator $Y(u)$ is positive.
